title: Form handling
summary: Read form fields on submit, check the values and show a message to the user.

quiz.q: Why do we call `event.preventDefault()` in a submit handler?
options: To stop the browser from reloading the page when the form is sent
To make the form submit faster
quiz.explain: By default a submitted form makes the browser navigate away or reload. `preventDefault()` cancels that so your JavaScript can handle the data.

quiz.q: The user typed 25 into `<input id="age" type="number">`. What does this program print?
quiz.explain: An input's `value` is always a string, even for number fields. Convert it with `Number(...)` before comparing sizes.

quiz.q: Which expression removes spaces from both ends of the text typed in `field`?
quiz.explain: `trim()` is a string method. It is a good habit to trim user input before checking it, so a box containing only spaces counts as empty.

quiz.q: Complete the listener that runs when the form is submitted.
quiz.explain: Listen for `submit` on the form, not `click` on the button. That also covers pressing Enter inside a field.

quiz.q: Click the line with the mistake. The goal is to reject ages below 18.
quiz.explain: The condition is reversed. It reports an error for adults. It should be `age < 18`.
